mainTopic: Using a מיגו to collect a debt from orphans' land, and an heir's claim to past produce after the other side admits
overview: This amud finishes the story of רבא בר שרשום. He held land from the orphans' father as collateral (משכנתא). He wanted to keep using it to collect a second, unsecured debt without a שבועה, relying on a מיגו: he could have claimed he bought the land. אביי rejects this, because everyone knows the land belongs to the orphans, so 'I bought it' would never have been believed. He must return the land and sue the orphans once they grow up. The גמרא then tells a new story: רב אידי בר אבין and another man each claim to be the closer relative of a man who died and left a date palm. When the other man admits רב אידי is closer, רב חסדא gives him the tree. רב חסדא refuses to make the other man pay for the dates he already ate, because רב אידי's only proof is that man's admission, and until then he claimed the opposite. The amud ends by noting that אביי and רבא disagree with רב חסדא, and their reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The background: a second debt and the end of the collateral years
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר שרשום finishes describing the facts. The orphans' father also owed him other money, and he has already used the land for the agreed years of the משכנתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father also owed me other money, and I already profited from the land for the full years of the collateral.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר שרשום is finishing his explanation to אביי of why he is still holding the orphans' land. These are the facts that set up his reasoning in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two debts. The first was secured by the land as a משכנתא, and its time is now up. The second debt had no collateral at all, and that is the debt he now wants to collect.

keyTerms.meaning: Other money, meaning a separate debt
A collateral arrangement where the lender uses the land for a set number of years
Literally 'I ate it'; I used up its produce

phrases.english: other money with him,
phrases.notes: רבא בר שרשום is still talking: the orphans' father also owed him a second debt, separate from the collateral deal.

phrases.english: and I profited from it for the years of the collateral.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא בר שרשום's answer to אביי, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Factual setup: the collateral years are finished, and there is still a separate unsecured debt.

steps.title: רבא בר שרשום's reasoning: keep the land using a מיגו
steps.stepSummary: If he returns the land and sues, he would need a שבועה to collect from orphans. So he plans to hide the collateral document and keep eating the land's produce. He argues he is believed because of a מיגו: he could have claimed he bought the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: I thought: if I give the land back to the orphans and tell them their father owes me more money, the Sages say that anyone collecting from orphans' property needs an oath. So instead I will hide the collateral document and keep using the land until I have collected what I am owed. Since I could have just said 'I bought this land' and been believed, I am also believed when I say 'you owe me money.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר שרשום explains why he decided to keep the land instead of giving it back. He relies on a מיגו, the rule that a person is believed in a claim if he could have made a stronger claim and been believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collecting from יתומים normally needs a שבועה, which he wanted to avoid. He reasons that because he has used the land for years, he could claim it was a purchase (חזקה), and that would be believed. So his smaller claim, that he is owed money, should also be believed.

keyTerms.meaning: One who comes to collect a debt from orphans' property
I will hide it away (literally 'press it down')
'Since': a claim is believed because the person could have made a stronger claim
It is bought, and that is why it is in my hand

steps.confusionAlert: He is not saying he really bought the land. He admits it was only collateral. He is only saying he COULD have claimed a purchase, and he wants that possible claim to back up his true claim of a debt.

phrases.aramaic: אָמֵינָא: אִי מַהְדַּרְנָא לַהּ אַרְעָא לְיַתְמֵי,
phrases.english: I said: If I return the land to the orphans,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמֵינָא דְּאִית לִי זוּזִי אַחֲרִינֵי גַּבֵּי דַּאֲבוּכוֹן –
phrases.english: and I say that I have other money with your father –
the Sages said:
one who comes to collect from the property of orphans –
may collect only with an oath.
Rather, I will hide the collateral document,
and profit from it up to the amount of the money,
since, if I wanted, I could say
'It is bought, that is why it is in my hand' – and I would be believed,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָמֵינָא דְּאִית לִי זוּזִי גַּבַּיְיכוּ – מְהֵימַנְנָא.
phrases.english: so when I say that I have money owed by you – I am believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמֵינָא: אִי מַהְדַּרְנָא לַהּ אַרְעָא לְיַתְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the facts in step 1 to explain why he kept the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא בר שרשום claims he may collect his unsecured debt from the land without a שבועה, based on a מיגו of 'I bought it.'

steps.title: אביי: the מיגו fails because everyone knows it is orphans' land
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the reasoning. The claim 'I bought it' could never have worked, because there is a known rumor (קלא) that the land belongs to the orphans. Without a believable stronger claim, there is no מיגו.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: You could not have said 'I bought it,' because it is well known that this land belongs to the orphans.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רבא בר שרשום's argument. A מיגו only works if the stronger claim would really have been believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole מיגו rested on 'I could have claimed a purchase.' Since the public already knows the land is the orphans', a purchase claim would not have been accepted. So the מיגו falls away, and he has no grounds to keep the land and collect from it without a שבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: You are not able to say

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key limit of מיגו: it only works if the stronger claim would really have been believed. A known public fact can cancel the stronger claim.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: אביי is answering רבא בר שרשום.

phrases.english: 'It is bought, in my hand' you are not able to say –
since there is a public rumor about it
that it is the orphans' land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְקוּחָה בְּיָדִי לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the מיגו argument of step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the entire basis for keeping the land: the מיגו.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The stronger claim ('I bought it') would not have been believed because of the public קלא that the land belongs to the orphans.

steps.title: אביי's instruction: return the land and sue later
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רבא בר שרשום to give the land back now and take the orphans to court once they are grown up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Instead, go give the land back to them, and when the orphans grow up, take them to court.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the מיגו, אביי tells רבא בר שרשום what he must actually do. This closes the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he has no valid reason to keep the land, it goes back to the יתומים right away. His debt claim is not cancelled. He just has to bring it to court when the orphans are adults.

keyTerms.meaning: Speak in judgment, meaning go to court

steps.whatToRemember: A lender holding orphans' land as collateral cannot keep it past the agreed term for a separate debt by using a מיגו of 'I bought it,' since everyone knows it is the orphans' land. He must return it and sue when they grow up.

phrases.english: Rather, go return it to them,
and when the orphans grow up –
litigate with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical result of the rejection in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The land must be returned to the orphans now, and the debt may be claimed in court once they are adults.

steps.title: A new story: two men each claim to be the closer relative
steps.stepSummary: A relative of רב אידי בר אבין died and left a date palm. רב אידי and another man each claim to be the closer relative, which would make him the heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: A relative of רב אידי בר אבין died and left a date palm. רב אידי בר אבין said, 'I am the closer relative,' and another man said, 'I am the closer relative.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story with a new case. This step sets out the dispute, and the ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heir is whoever is the closer relative. Each side makes the same claim, so at this point nothing decides between them.

phrases.aramaic: קְרִיבֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין שְׁכֵיב,
phrases.english: A relative of Rav Idi bar Avin died,
and left a date palm.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר: אֲנָא קָרִיבְנָא טְפֵי;
phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said: I am the closer relative;

phrases.aramaic: וְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא אֲמַר: אֲנָא קָרִיבְנָא טְפֵי.
phrases.english: and that man said: I am the closer relative.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְרִיבֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין שְׁכֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new, separate story after the end of the רבא בר שרשום case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up an inheritance dispute where both sides claim to be the closer relative.

steps.title: The other man admits, and רב חסדא gives the tree to רב אידי
steps.stepSummary: The other man finally admits that רב אידי בר אבין is the closer relative, so רב חסדא places the date palm in רב אידי's possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, the other man admitted to him that רב אידי was the closer relative, so רב חסדא put the tree in רב אידי's possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The dispute is settled by the other man's own admission. רב חסדא rules that the tree belongs to רב אידי בר אבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other man's admission ends the disagreement, because his own words now support רב אידי's claim. רב חסדא acts on that admission and gives the inheritance to רב אידי.

keyTerms.meaning: Established it in his hand, meaning gave him possession

phrases.aramaic: לְסוֹף אוֹדִי לֵיהּ דְּאִיהוּ קָרִיב טְפֵי,
phrases.english: In the end he admitted to him that he was the closer relative,
phrases.notes: The other man is admitting that רב אידי is the closer one.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda established it in his possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְסוֹף אוֹדִי לֵיהּ דְּאִיהוּ קָרִיב טְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the dispute set up in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Based on the other man's admission, רב חסדא gives the date palm to רב אידי בר אבין.

steps.title: רב אידי demands the past produce
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין asks רב חסדא to make the other man pay back all the dates he ate from the tree until now.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי said to רב חסדא: Let him give me back the produce he ate from that day until now!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that he has won the tree, רב אידי בר אבין asks for more. He wants the other man to repay the fruit he ate while he held the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אידי's claim is that if the tree was really his all along, the fruit was his too. So the other man ate fruit that did not belong to him and should pay for it.

keyTerms.meaning: produce, fruit (here the dates from the palm)

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב אידי בר אבין is speaking to רב חסדא.

phrases.english: Let him return to me the produce
that he ate from that day until now!
phrases.notes: "That day" means the day the other man first took the tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ruling in Step 6 and adds a new demand for the past produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אידי claims that he is owed the value of all the fruit the other man ate since he took the tree.

steps.title: רב חסדא rejects the demand for produce
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא is surprised at רב אידי. His ownership rests only on the other man's admission, and that man was saying until now that he himself was closer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Is this the one people call a great man? On whom are you relying? On this man! But until now he was saying, "I am closer!"
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא pushes back sharply. He says רב אידי has no right to the past produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אידי won the tree only because the other man admitted it. That admission speaks only from the moment it was made. Before that, the same man was claiming he was the closer heir, so it cannot be used to make him pay for the past.

keyTerms.meaning: a great man, an important scholar

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not saying the tree doesn't belong to רב אידי. He still owns it. רב חסדא is only refusing to give him the fruit from the time before the admission.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that ownership proven only by someone's admission may start from the time of the admission, not earlier. The next step shows that אביי and רבא disagree with this ruling of רב חסדא.

phrases.english: He said:
Is this the one about whom they say
"He is a great man"?
On whom is the master relying?
On this one;
phrases.notes: He means the other man's admission is your only proof.

phrases.english: but he was saying
"I am closer"!

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הוּא שֶׁאוֹמְרִים עָלָיו אָדָם גָּדוֹל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects רב אידי's demand from Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the demand for past produce. רב אידי still owns the tree.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The only proof of ownership is the other man's admission, and until he admitted it he claimed the opposite. So the admission cannot reach back into the past.

steps.title: אביי and רבא disagree with רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that אביי and רבא do not hold like this ruling of רב חסדא. The explanation follows next.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא do not agree with this ruling of רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us that אביי and רבא disagree with רב חסדא, and it is about to explain how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we only had רב חסדא's view. The גמרא is opening a new point by saying that other אמוראים rule differently. Their reasoning comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: they do not hold, they disagree

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava
do not hold
this ruling of Rav Chisda,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא לָא סְבִירָא לְהוּ הָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces disagreement with רב חסדא's handling of the date palm case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי and רבא do not accept רב חסדא's ruling. The details follow in the next section.
